title: Async window-splitter writes shadow KV slots causing softmax divergence on long prefixes
creator: Maya Chen
description: After landing the async window-splitter optimization to break very long prefill sequences into parallel split windows, we observed subtle numerical divergences in softmax outputs for long-prefix generation under certain concurrency patterns. The divergence manifests as shifted probability mass (token-ranking changes) after ~512+ tokens on models using mixed precision and speculative splitting. This ticket tracks investigation, reproducer, mitigation, and fix for correctness regression introduced by the splitter optimization.
reproducer_steps: Checkout runtime-1.20 branch with async-window-splitter enabled
Start local node with GPU (A100) and set PREFILL_WINDOW=256, SPLIT_THRESHOLD=1024
Run perf_regression_repro.py with model redwood-13b, seed 42, batch_size=1, max_new_tokens=2048, mixed_precision=fp16
Compare logits sequence-by-sequence against baseline runtime-1.19 on the same input; divergence usually appears between token 512..900
Trigger under moderate concurrency: spawn 4 concurrent decode workers against same model to increase race probability
logs_snippet:
[2025-02-12T14:03:21Z] prefiller: window-splitter: created split id=0x7f8a2 shadow_write(slot=12345)
[2025-02-12T14:03:21Z] decoder-worker-3: read_kv(slot=12345) -> values mismatch checksum=0x9a7b vs baseline=0x2c3d
[2025-02-12T14:03:21Z] softmax: sum=0.998732 (baseline 0.999991) -> probability shift observed
investigation_summary: Initial triage indicates a timing window where the splitter writes a temporary 'shadow' KV slab entry while migrating tokens between split windows. If a concurrent decoder thread reads the KV slab during an incomplete write (non-atomic on the chosen memory layout), the read can return partially-updated vectors. Those partial values, when reduced in mixed-precision softmax paths, amplify rounding error and shift normalization causing token-rank changes. The bug surface is rare and correlated with: (1) high prefill length, (2) split happening close to slab boundary, (3) mixed-precision kernels (fp16/amp) and (4) concurrent decoder activity.
root_cause_hypothesis: The window-splitter's migration path uses a non-atomic two-stage write: allocate shadow slots, copy slices, then swap metadata pointer. On CUDA kernels optimized for coalesced writes we dropped an explicit memory-fence/atomic-swap on the KV index update. Concurrent readers may observe the shadow slot contents before the metadata swap completes, leading to partially-initialized vectors being used in softmax. Mixed-precision accumulation in the softmax kernel magnifies the numerical discrepancy into observable token selection differences.
proposed_fix: Make KV migration atomic from reader perspective: (A) write shadow slot, (B) issue an ordered device-side fence, (C) perform atomic CAS on KV index metadata, and (D) expose a short reader backoff when an in-flight migration flag is set. Update the splitter to mark slots as INVALID until fully initialized and ensure readers treat INVALID as a cache miss that triggers fallback to stable slot. Add unit tests that inject read-write preemption to assert no partial reads.
mitigations: Backout async-window-splitter toggle in runtime-1.20 for safety release if we cannot patch quickly
Enable conservative fence path via env flag WINDOW_SPLITTER_SAFE=1 for affected customers
Limit concurrent decode workers per model instance until fix is validated
temporary_workaround: Set WINDOW_SPLITTER_ENABLED=0 or WINDOW_SPLITTER_SAFE=1 on deployments with long-prefill workloads. As a targeted workaround for Dedicated customers, set PREFILL_SPLIT_THRESHOLD=2048 to avoid splits for typical workloads.
